title: Network partition tolerance and local-fallback playbook for private deploys
author: Ravi Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes strategies and concrete operator steps for handling network partitions and control-plane loss in Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers automated degraded-mode behaviors, detection heuristics, safe local-fallback operation, and rollback/rollback-avoidance procedures for customers running inference behind a private control plane or with hybrid connectivity to Redwood. The procedures prioritize customer data sovereignty, inference availability, and safe evidence capture for post-incident analysis.

Intended audience

- Field operators and SREs responsible for private deployments
- Solutions engineers coordinating customer cutovers
- Customer on-call engineers during an incident

Goals and scope

- Maintain inference availability for critical tenants during WAN/control-plane interruptions
- Ensure predictable degradation with documented SLO impact and telemetry
- Provide reversible operator actions with minimal state loss risk
- Specify testable acceptance criteria and rollback guidance

Key concepts and terminology

- Local-fallback mode: runtime switches to a self-contained serving topology (no control-plane dependency) that serves pinned model artifacts and a reduced feature set for safety and predictability.
- Control-plane partition: loss of connectivity between customer site and Redwood control plane (partial or full) that prevents policy, quota, or model catalog updates.
- Degraded SLOs: pre-defined, acceptable thresholds for latency, throughput, and error rates when in local-fallback. Example targets: p95 latency <= 1200 ms (short requests), availability >= 98% for critical routes.

Detection and automatic triggers

1) Primary detectors (runtime + agent):
   - Control-plane heartbeat missed for 3 consecutive cycles (default 30s per cycle).
   - Agent telemetry shows >50% of API calls returning control-plane-403/504 across 2 minutes.
   - Network monitor detects BGP route withdrawal or private interconnect health degraded to <30% packet success.

2) Secondary detectors (observability signals):
   - Sudden spike in cache-miss rate for model artifacts (+80% relative change).
   - Quota reconciliation failures in audit logs with timestamps matching heartbeat loss.

3) Automated trigger policy (example):
   - If (PrimaryDetector AND (SecondaryDetector OR operator-ack)) for 120s then transition runtime -> local-fallback.

Automated local-fallback behavior (what the runtime does)

- Freeze model catalog and pin currently active model versions.
- Switch to read-only token validation using cached keys; reject new token issuances that require control-plane approval.
- Disable non-essential features: dynamic routing, fleet-wide batching policies, live-rollout A/B policies.
- Serve with conservative batch sizing and KV cache TTL extension to reduce upstream dependency.
- Emit a high-fidelity incident event to the local bus and persistent evidence bundle (see Evidence collection).

Operator runbook (step-by-step)

Pre-incident preparation (operator checklist)

- Ensure operator playbook runbook role assigned and reachable (pager group: #private-deploy-ops).
- Confirm last successful artifact hash + model metadata stored in /opt/redwood/artifacts/manifest and replicated to N+1 local storage.
- Validate local time sync (NTP) and certificate validity for cached token keys.
- Smoke test local-fallback in a staging subsite monthly: run the synthetic workload in lab and verify degraded SLOs.

Immediate response (0–10 minutes)

1) Triage and confirm partition:
   a) Check control-plane heartbeat: curl --fail https://controlplane.internal.redwood/ping || true
   b) Confirm BGP/Interconnect: ip route show && ping -c 5 <control-plane-ip>
   c) Check agent logs: sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent --since "10 minutes ago" | grep "heartbeat"

2) If automated fallback has NOT triggered and partition persists >120s, manually engage local-fallback:
   - CLI: redwood-runtime transition --mode local-fallback --reason "detected-network-partition"
   - Confirm transition: redwood-runtime status | grep Mode

3) If automated fallback is active, validate functionality:
   - Run smoke queries: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' | jq .
   - Check SLO telemetry: promql: rate(requests_total{route=~"critical.*"}[5m]) and p95 latency dashboards

Stabilization (10–60 minutes)

- Reduce non-critical traffic: apply temporary rate-limits for batch routes via local config:

YAML example (local runtime config):
---
inference:
  routes:
    critical:
      max_qps: 50
    batch:
      enabled: false
  cache:
    kv_ttl_sec: 3600
    prefix_cache: true
---

- Enable graceful degradation feature: serve summarized responses (structured outputs only) for long-running prompts to keep token costs predictable.
- If spot/ephemeral GPUs are in use, pin inference to persistent pools to avoid cold-eviction during partition.

Rollback and incrementally restoring normal operation (once connectivity returns)

- Controlled rejoin checklist:
  1) Verify network path restored (sustained success ping/control-plane API responses for 5 minutes).
  2) Confirm control-plane accepts runtime heartbeat and token reconciliation succeeds (run: redwood-agent reconcile --dry-run).
  3) Dry-run staged policy updates in a canary group (10% traffic) and monitor for errors for 10 minutes.
  4) Gradually re-enable features: batch routes -> dynamic routing -> remote rollouts. Leave model swap disabled until artifact integrity verified.

- If rejoin produces policy conflicts (e.g., mismatched quotas or model hashes):
  - Pause global rollout.
  - Create an evidence bundle: /var/lib/redwood/evidence/<incident-id>.tar.gz and upload to secure evidence bucket with signed metadata.
  - Coordinate with customer security contact before force-syncing policy changes.

Evidence collection and post-incident analysis

- Automatically collected artifacts (local-fallback):
  - runtime-status.json (dump of active model pins and route config)
  - agent-heartbeat.log (last 30 minutes)
  - packet-capture summary (if enabled) – pcap trimmed to 2MB
  - prom metrics snapshot (prometheus_exporter.tar.gz)

- Manual evidence checklist for operator:
  1) Ensure logs preserved: sudo tar czf evidence.tar.gz /var/log/redwood/* /opt/redwood/artifacts/manifest
  2) Note timeline and trigger points in incident timeline template (include UTC timestamps).
  3) Tag incident with confidentiality level and customer approval status before sharing with product/security.

Testing and validation matrix

- Monthly chaos test scenarios (recommended):
  - Partial control-plane loss (simulate 50% control-plane pods unavailable): validate automated fallback triggers and recovery window <4m.
  - Complete WAN outage for customer site (simulate blackhole): validate local-fallback availability >=98% and data retention behavior.
  - Rejoin with mismatched model hash: validate evidence bundling and rollback protection prevents silent overwrites.

- Acceptance criteria for staged test:
  - Local-fallback activates within 180s for deterministic triggers.
  - No customer data leaves the site during standby fallback (verify telemetry sampling settings).
  - Rejoin completes without data loss and with operator-acknowledged policy reconcile.

Operational metrics to monitor (examples)

- controlplane_heartbeat_failures_total (alert threshold > 5 in 5m)
- runtime_mode{mode="local-fallback"} (count of nodes)
- requests_p95_ms{deployed_env="private"} (alert if >1200ms for critical routes)
- artifact_cache_hit_ratio (keep >90% during fallback)
- evidence_bundle_created (event)

Escalation and communication templates

- Pager escalation: contact #private-deploy-ops -> oncall lead -> customer success SLA owner.
- Customer-facing update template (first 30 mins):
  Subject: Incident: Private deploy network partition (ID: {{incident_id}})
  Body: We detected a network partition at {{time}} UTC. Runtime has entered a local-fallback mode to maintain inference availability for your critical routes. Impact: degraded latency and reduced feature set. Next update: {{time+30m}} UTC.

Configuration examples and safe-guards

- Sample runtime guard (policy fragment):
  - name: local_fallback_window
    type: timer
    params: {"trigger_secs": 120, "required_signals": ["heartbeat_miss", "bgp_withdrawal"]}

- Safe-guard: operator-confirmed model swap protection (default: true). This prevents any model-version advance while local-fallback is active unless operator explicitly approves:
  redwood-runtime config set safety.model_swap_allowed false

Related pages and references

- See also: tenant-state-snapshot-coordination-and-operator-checklist-2027 (day-2 ops)
- Test harness: eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/offline-upgrade-validation-harness-and-simulated-workload-suite-2026

Appendix A — Incident timeline template (copy into ticket)

1) Detection timestamp (UTC)
2) Triggering signals (list)
3) Automated actions taken by runtime
4) Manual operator actions (commands + who)
5) Recovery timestamp and verification steps
